recentItems.title: Rome weighs fines for ‘distracted walkers’
recentItems.description:
If you don’t watch where you’re going, it’s going to cost you — at least in Italy. 

The country is proposing a fine, equal to about $120 Cdn, for pedestrians caught staring at their phones while crossing the road. Italian courts have already started holding distracted pedestrians at least partially responsible for accidents. It’s hoped a fine will discourage this type of behaviour.
